Welcome to The Castle School
Together, we transform lives through education. We empower every student to achieve, belong, and participate, with an unwavering commitment to creating equitable opportunities and prioritising under-resourced students.
The Houses are essential in fostering the strong family ethos at The Castle School. We very much believe in the partnership between parents and the school. The House system enables us to work with our families; siblings always go into the same House so we get to know families over time.
We are hugely proud of our school and the achievements of our students, in particular within the Creative Arts and Sports. At The Castle School, we value strong positive relationships and this alongside the history and tradition of The Castle School makes the school such a vibrant and lively place to work.
Rated as Outstanding by Ofsted, we have been for some years now at the top of the performance tables in Somerset and the South West, while also comparing well to schools nationally for academic achievements. You can see our latest exam results on our website.
This must be supported by a curriculum that gives students the power to think for themselves, shaped by what they need to know, understand and fulfil, in order to have happy, successful and prosperous lives.
The safety of our students is paramount. At The Castle School we take our duty to safeguard and promote the welfare of children extremely seriously. Please visit our Safeguarding page for more information.
Please take a look at The Castle Magazine and see all the amazing things our students have been doing; it's a wonderful reflection of the last academic year and really demonstrates the commitment to our aim that every child achieves, belongs and participates.
We look forward to your family being part of our success.
Mr Jamie Wordsworth, Headteacher

pageCache.pageTitle: Ethos and Values — The Castle School
pageCache.text:
Our Ethos and Values
Our mission – Why do we exist?
Together, we transform lives through education.
We empower every student to achieve, belong, and participate, with an unwavering commitment to creating equitable opportunities and prioritising under-resourced students.
The Houses are essential in fostering the strong family ethos at The Castle School. We very much believe in the partnership between parents and the school. The House system enables us to work with our families; siblings always go into the same House so we get to know families over time.
Integrity | Humility | Generosity
We work hard on the things that matter, and our mission and values are aligned, knowing the things that matter are the right things.
We are kind to each other, and we show humility.
We are professionally generous enabling others to benefit from our work and keen to collaborate.
Achieve - ‘Knowledge enables students to think the unthinkable and the not yet thought’ (Bernstein)
High expectations – Outstanding outcomes Plus One
Ambitious curriculum and powerful knowledge
Belong - ‘Belonging is a flame that needs to be continually fed by signals of connection’ (Coyle)
Exceptional pastoral care
Participate - ‘Equality of opportunity is the essence of social justice’ (Honore)
Enrichment - Universal/Choice/Targeted
Sustained participation
Personal Development
Volunteering/ Servitude
Every Child a Reader – Robust and early identification of reading levels and effective intervention to support students at the early stages of reading. Reading opportunities and disciplinary literacy are built into the curriculum and implemented consistently by colleagues.
Attendance and Lost Learning
Attendance – Students attend well and can fully engage in their learning.
Lost learning – Address lost learning due to all forms of absence.
Adaptive teaching for SEND - Lesson activities and interventions support vulnerable students with additional practice, tailored support and acquiring component knowledge.
We connect with each other, our students and communities by building strong relationships that create a joyful, rigorous, high performing school.
We are relentless where nothing is left to chance and we promote a culture of no surprises.
As adults we model ‘how we behave’ in every interaction we have.
We have strategic anchors focused on:
Curriculum – Our aim is to provide a curriculum that is highly effective in delivering GCSE outcomes and ensures our students will be widely educated
People – Our talent is our most valuable resource
Equity – We believe this is the essence of social justice

pageCache.pageTitle: Blackdown Education Partnership — The Castle School
pageCache.text:
The Castle School is a member of the Blackdown Education Partnership - a partnership of schools working as a Multi-Academy Trust across Devon and Somerset.
Our shared mission is to deliver excellent education for all our pupils (aged 2-18 years) so they go on to fulfil their potential, lead safe happy lives and make a positive contribution to society.
The aims of the Trust is to create and support a network of exceptional schools where:
each school within the Trust sits at the heart of its community
aspirations and expectations are high, and achievable, for everyone
the culture is joyful and children and staff enjoy coming to work and learn
Full information about the Trust, can be found on the Blackdown Education Partnership Website
Members
Members oversee the work of the Trust and are responsible for overarching decisions, such as changing the Trust’s Articles of Association, and the appointment of Directors and Governors. Our Members subscribed to the formation of the Trust and meet the obligations set out in our Articles of Association.
Members hold Directors and the Board to account, and in this way ensure that the Trust is working to best effect.
Trustees
Trustees are appointed by our Members to take responsibility for the strategic direction of the Trust, working in the way that a Board oversees a company or charity.
Local Governing Committees
Each School has their own Local Governing Committee (LGC) which provides immediate oversight of the school for the Trust.
LGCs are made up of Governors who are recruited locally. Their work resembles that of the governing bodies of maintained schools and is set within the vision, values and policies defined by the Trust.
For more information about our school’s Local Governing Committee, please click here.
Trust Address and Contact Details
Blackdown Education PartnershipChapel Hill, Uffculme, Devon, EX15 3AG
Website: www.bep.acEmail: admin@bep.acPhone: 01884 842900

Blackdown Education Partnership believes in the potential of every child
Our Mission: Belief in Every Child
To deliver an exceptional educational experience in schools where all children succeed
Our Values: Equity, Opportunity, Community
Schools and Academies within the Trust
Latest News
Term has started well in our Trust. We had some excellent summer outcomes across our schools including for disadvantaged pupils. All of our primary schools are currently above the national average for attendance, and our secondaries are all significantly ahead of last year’s data, with some also above national.
We are delighted to welcome Clyst Vale Community College as they formally become part of our Trust today. They will join us in sharing our moral mission:
• To nurture and develop the ambition, talents and interests of every child​
• To break down the barriers that inhibit the opportunities and achievements of disadvantaged pupils so that they can go on to lead lives of choice and opportunity​
• To create a family of schools that are deeply and purposefully connected to their communities. #beliefineverychild
Hats off and thank you to our colleagues who have been through Ofsted under this new framework. There is no doubt that the bar is so much higher than under the old framework and achieving the expected standard is a significant success.
Blackdown Education Partnership (BEP), in cooperation with Somerset Council, is consulting on a proposal to make a significant organisational change to existing SEND provision within the Wellington locality.
The aim is to provide specialist provision on a mainstream site, where appropriate, pupils will have opportunities to access mainstream learning and facilities as part of a bespoke approach.
Blackdown Education Partnership and The Oak Partnership Trust in cooperation with Somerset County Council are consulting on a proposal to make a significant organisational change to existing SEND provision within the Wellington Community. This relates to a proposal to transfer The Cove which is currently operated by Selworthy School to an intergrated SEND unit hosted at Court Fields School. Further information can be found here
A particular highlight of this term has been the transfer of Tiverton High School to the Trust and so I would like to whole heartedly welcome all the staff of Tiverton to BEP. We are delighted to have you on the team and look forward very much to supporting the school to become a brilliant part of the Tiverton community in the months and years to come.
We are delighted to welcome Tiverton High School as they formally become part of our Trust today. They will join us in sharing our moral mission:
• To nurture and develop the ambition, talents and interests of every child​
• To break down the barriers that inhibit the opportunities and achievements of disadvantaged pupils so that they can go on to lead lives of choice and opportunity​
• To create a family of schools that are deeply and purposefully connected to their communities. #beliefineverychild
I am so proud of the uniqueness of the schools in BEP; how each one truly reflects their community and it is brilliant to celebrate this diversity both within and between our schools. Yet there are common threads that bind us together: kindness, inclusivity, opportunity and a fierce ambition for every child.
Please find attached information regarding the proposal to extend the age range at Holyrood Academy and add primary provision with a nursery.
Thank you to all colleagues for your hard work over the first (and longest) half term of the academic year. Thanks to you, attendance is up, suspensions are down and our children continue to enjoy great relationships with staff and each other, increasingly fantastic facilities, excellent teaching and a range of exciting, challenging and fun opportunities.

pageCache.pageTitle: SEND Information Report — The Castle School
pageCache.text:
SEND Information Report
Please click here to view our most recent SEND Information Report

Careers
Careers Information
As part of our commitment to careers education, The Castle School will:
Provide students with access to up to date, relevant and impartial careers information, advice and guidance that supports their aspirations and helps prepare them for their next steps
Help students to develop the knowledge and skills needed to make informed decisions at key transition points and to participate in post 16 education and/or employment
Build career readiness through ensuring students have the skills, knowledge and behaviours required for the world of work
Delivering good careers education is a whole school responsibility. Our careers provision is integrated through Career Lessons and Activities, Enrichment Days, Tutor Time, PSHE and Class Assemblies; helping to ensure key learning outcomes and aims are achieved.
Careers Staff
For further information regarding the school’s Careers Programme, please contact:
Mrs Michelle Rolls (Careers Lead) mrolls@castle.bep.ac
Vacancy (Work Experience Coordinator)
Mr Darryl Simpson (SLT Careers Lead) office@castle.bep.ac
Mr Laurie Morgan (School Governor, focus Careers) office@castle.bep.ac
Careers Programme
Our Careers Programme is delivered through year 7 to year 11. Click here to view the Careers Programme for 2026-2027.
Provider Access Statement
The school is committed to ensuring that all students in Years 8 to 11 have access to information about the range of post 16 education and training opportunities available to them. During their time at school, students will have opportunities to engage with a variety of education and training providers; helping them to make informed choices about their next steps.
Our Provider Access Statement outlines how post 16 learning providers can engage with students in Years 8 to 11.
You can view our Provider Access Statement here.
Gatsby Benchmarks
Our Careers Programme is aligned with the Gatsby Benchmarks. We review and evaluate our careers provision against these benchmarks on a termly basis to ensure that it continues to meet statutory requirements and delivers positive outcomes for all students.
1 A stable careers programme
2 Learning from labour market information
3 Addressing the needs of every pupil
4 Linking curriculum to careers
5 Encounters with employers and employees
6 Experiences of the workplace
7 Encounters with further and higher education
You can learn more about The Gatsby Benchmarks here.
The Castle School works closely with the Somerset Careers Hub and is supported by a Careers and Enterprise Adviser from the Careers and Enterprise Company in the delivery and development of our Careers Programme and the achievement of the Gatsby Benchmarks.
More information about the Careers and Enterprise Company can be accessed here.
Personal Guidance Meetings
All students are seen by a qualified Careers Advisor whilst at school who provides impartial one to one information, advice, and guidance to support them with their career aspirations, future plans and next steps.
Students are seen in years 10/11 for an individual career guidance interview and will receive a copy of their meeting notes in the form of an action plan. Parents/carers are encouraged to support them in completing agreed next steps.
Parents/carers are welcome to attend their child’s careers interview. If you would like to be involved, please contact Miss Wishart at office@castle.bep.ac to arrange a mutually convenient appointment.
Useful Links
Below is a selection of useful websites and online resources to help students and parents/carers explore education, employment and training opportunities. Students and parents/carers are encouraged to explore these resources regularly.
Find an Apprenticeships Service
An online service for students to search and apply for apprenticeship opportunities.
Supported Internships
Supported Internships are work based study programmes for young people aged 16 to 24 with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) who have and an Education, Health and Care (EHC) plan.
Skill Up Somerset offer free, impartial advice and guidance on skills, training and apprenticeship opportunities across Somerset.
Careers and Enterprise Padlet
The Student Padlet provides regular updates on local opportunities, events and resources to support careers education and planning for future pathways.
The National Careers Service
The National Careers Service provides confidential information, advice and guidance to help people make decisions about employment, education and training.
Choosing the right subjects to study post 16 can be very important for accessing certain university courses, particularly a Russell Group University. Informed Choices provides guidance to help students make informed decisions about their post 16 options and future progression routes.
Local Further Education & Training Providers
Below is a list of local colleges and training providers that students might wish to consider for post 16 study. We encourage students and parents/carers to visit provider websites and attend open days and information events to explore the facilities, find out more about available courses, entry requirements and progression opportunities.
University Centre Somerset College Group
Richard Huish College
Somerset Skills & Learning
Labour Market Information (LMI)
Students are encouraged to use Labour Market Information (LMI) to make informed decisions about post 16 education, employment and training.
Labour market information provides valuable insights into local and national career opportunities, including growth sectors, salary expectations and qualification and skill requirements. Students, parents and carers are encouraged to use Learning from Career and Labour Market Information and Careerometer.
Information for Families
Parents and carers play a key role in supporting young people with their career planning and next step preparation. Regular conversations exploring education, employment and training options can help students to feel more informed and confident about their next steps.
The resources below provide valuable information to support discussions at home.
Choosing KS4 Options
Information to help students and their families understand KS4 option choices and how they can link to future education, employment and training
Companies with Apprenticeships
Useful resource listing employers who offer apprenticeship programmes and general information on apprenticeships
Information on the range of pathways available after year 11, including: T Levels, A Levels, Apprenticeships, Foundation Apprenticeships, Supported Internships and Apprenticeships and BTECs
Information on higher education, apprenticeships, employment, gap years and other progression routes available
Resources for Choosing Which Career
Useful websites with tools and activities to help students explore interests, understand job roles and plan for the future
Somerset Careers Hub | Facebook
Follow Somerset Careers Hub on Facebook to view valuable information to help support your child in making informed choices
How Families can help
We value the support that parents and carers can bring to our Careers Programme and offer a range of opportunities to get involved. By sharing your knowledge, experience and insights you can help students to develop a greater understanding of the world of work and the wide range of opportunities available to them.
We welcome support from parents/carers across a range of activities, including:
Career talks and presentations
Employer led projects and assignments
Workplace visits and tasters
Work experience placements
Supporting curriculum learning through industry talks
If you would like to support our Careers Programme or find out more about how you can get involved, please contact us at office@castle.bep.co.uk.
Information for Teachers
Subject teachers are highly influential in supporting students to make informed decisions about their future education, employment and training pathways. Careers education should be embedded across all subjects, helping students to understand the relevance of the subject they are learning. By making links between curriculum learning and the world of work, teachers can help to raise aspirations and broaden students’ understanding of the opportunities available to them.
Connect subject learning to the essential employability skills. Actively practise and aim to develop these skills. Celebrate students that do these things well.
Discuss careers and pathways related to your subject. Talk to your students about their next steps.
Keep up to date with developments in post 16 education, qualifications and workplace training, especially local opportunities.
Talk to students about how employment is changing; careers of the future and those in decline.
Play videos of people from various backgrounds talking about their careers linking to your subject.
Use case studies of successful and/or famous people from a range of backgrounds working in your subject.
Challenge stereotypes of people working and learning in your field.
Invite former students back to your class to talk about working and/or studying in subject.
Make a display about careers and further learning related to your subject.
Link subject learning to the real world and industry so learners understand the connection. Connect with local businesses to make meaningful links between your subject and industry.
Introduce a careers element to trips; for example, by asking adults to explain their job and their pathway into it.
Teachers can find further help and support here.
Information for Employers
Employers play an important role in helping to prepare our students for future employment, education and training. Providing meaningful opportunities for young people to develop their knowledge and understanding of the world of work and career opportunities, alongside the key skills needed for employment, is a priority for the school.
We welcome support from employers across a range of activities, including:
Career talks and presentations
Employer led projects and assignments
Workplace visits and tasters
Work experience placements
Supporting curriculum learning through industry talks
If you would like to support our Careers Programme or find out more about how you can get involved, please contact us at office@castle.bep.co.uk.
Information for Alumni
We value the success of our former students and welcome Alumni into the school to support our Careers Programme. If you are a former student and would like to support our Careers Programme or find out more about how you can get involved, please contact us at office@castle.bep.co.uk.
Destination Data
Our student destination data can be viewed here. This data shows the percentage of students staying in education/training or going into employment after key stage 4. The Castle School regularly reviews and evaluates student destination data to develop and improve the impact of our Careers Programme.
Feedback Welcome
Feedback is actively sought from students, parents, carers, employers and teachers following all careers activity. This feedback is evaluated and used to inform and improve our Careers Programme. Please contact us at office@castle.bep.ac if you’d like to give any feedback.

Admissions
Year 6/7 Admissions Process
The admissions process for school place applications for September 2027 is now underway. The online portal for secondary school applications opened on 14 September 2026. The closing date for applications was 31 October 2026, and National Offer Day is 1 March 2027.
Further information, including how to apply for a secondary school place, can be found on the Somerset Council website: Applying for school (somerset.gov.uk). Parents and carers are strongly advised to read the admissions information carefully before submitting an application.
We encourage families to submit their applications before the deadline to ensure they are considered as part of the normal admissions round.
Admission Policies

The Castle School Admissions Policy 2026-27

Admission Arrangements for 2028-29: Annual Consultation
Along with all other schools and academies, we are consulting on our admission arrangements for 2028-29. You are invited to look at the proposed new admission arrangements and to have your say on them.
Summary of Proposed Changes
TCS Admissions Policy 2028
Our proposed Arrangements are on our admission page and you can see all the admission arrangements at http://devon.cc/schoolpolicy
Further information is here: www.devon.gov.uk/admissionarrangements

You can comment at schoolsadmissionpolicy-mailbox@devon.gov.uk or by emailing admin@bep.ac

pageCache.pageTitle: Music Development Plan — The Castle School
pageCache.text:
Music Development Plan
The Castle School Music Development Plan Summary
Overview
Academic year covered: 2025–2026
Date published: September 2025
Date to be reviewed: August 2026
Music Lead: Nicholas Adams
School Leadership link: Jamie Wordsworth
Local Music Hub: Sound Foundation Somerset
Other partnerships: Peripatetic teachers, Music Hub, Local Primary Schools, external ensembles, theatre and concert venues
Part A: Curriculum Music
The Castle School delivers one hour of curriculum music weekly to all KS3 pupils, fully aligned with the National Curriculum and guided by the Model Music Curriculum (MMC).
Curriculum intent focuses on inclusion, musical skills development (listening, appraising, performing, composing), and exposure to a broad repertoire including Western Classical, world music and popular music.
The KS3 curriculum follows a structured sequence of 6 Schemes of Work per year, rotating to ensure equal access to specialist spaces and instruments. Pupils experience whole-class instrumental learning (keyboards, guitars, djembe, band instruments), sequencing software (Cubase, Dorico), singing, notation reading, and ensemble playing.
Music technology is embedded throughout: digital audio workstations, sampling, audio recording, quantisation, automation and composition software.
Accessibility & SEND: Learning is scaffolded using modelling, differentiated parts, layered ensembles, visual notation, and varied task entry points. Technology allows alternative access routes for pupils with physical/learning needs.
Qualifications offered: GCSE Music and BTEC pathways are available at KS4
Part B: Co-curricular Music
The school offers extensive co-curricular musical opportunities beyond timetabled lessons, supporting musical progression, community involvement and personal development.
Instrumental/vocal tuition: Free tuition for FSM pupils; subsidised or promoted options for others. Tuition available on brass, woodwind, strings, voice, drums, guitar and piano.
Ensembles: Choirs (mixed year groups), Orchestra, Mini Orchestra, Woodwind group, Steel Pan Group, Indonesian Gamelan workshops, Rock/Pop bands. Ensemble membership is open and free.
Progression opportunities: Students can borrow instruments, attend after-school rehearsals, and enter graded exams or performance events. Technology clubs support composition and production.
Facilities: 4 practice rooms, 2 classrooms with breakout spaces, digital mixing desk, PA system, microphones, MIDI keyboards, ukuleles, percussion, guitars and digital audio workstations.
Part C: Musical Experiences
The school provides rich musical experiences that broaden cultural understanding and support lifelong engagement in music.
Regular school performances: Christmas Concert, Community Concert, The Gig, School Musical, Summer Showcase. All students have opportunities to participate or support technically.
Live music experiences: All Year 7 pupils attend a professional musical theatre performance each year, with accompanying workshops (vocals, dance, props). Further trips take students to concerts, orchestras and theatres.
Visiting professionals: Royal Marines Band Service, National Youth Orchestra, Somerstage, ActionTrack, acapella groups, vocal coaches, composers/musicians deliver workshops.
In the Future
Strengthening alignment with MMC and expanding KS3 depth across composition, performance and technology.
Increasing instrument lesson uptake for all pupils.
Introducing new ensembles (e.g., contemporary music tech band, world music groups).
Expanding live experience opportunities including more cross-school and community events.
Developing further use of Cubase, sampling, notation software and recording studios.
Enhancing assessment through consistent video/audio evidence and trust-wide criteria.

Foundational Knowlegde
Reading, Writing, Oracy, and Numeracy
At The Castle School, we believe that reading, writing, oracy, and numeracy are the foundations of success across all subjects. Students make the strongest progress when school and home work together to support all of the above.
You do not need to be an expert teacher to help your child. Small, regular actions at home can make a significant difference to confidence, achievement and future opportunities.
Supporting Reading at Home
Reading is one of the most important things a young person can do to improve their learning.
Students who read regularly are more likely to:
Develop a wider vocabulary.
Improve their comprehension skills.
Become more confident learners.
Achieve well across the curriculum.
Enjoy greater success in exams.
Encourage your child to read daily.
Ask them about what they are reading.
Read alongside them where appropriate.
Encourage them to borrow books from the school library.
Support completion of Sparx Reader homework.
Discuss new words and their meanings.
Model reading yourself whenever possible.
Questions you could ask
What happened in today's tutor time reading?
What new words have you learnt?
What do you think might happen next?
What is the main message of the text?
Supporting Vocabulary Development
A strong vocabulary helps students understand lessons, access exam questions and communicate effectively.
Encouraging curiosity about new words.
Talking about unfamiliar vocabulary encountered in books, television programmes and everyday life.
Discussing word origins and meanings.
Encouraging students to use ambitious vocabulary in conversation.
A few minutes of discussion each week can have a significant impact on language development.
Reading for Enjoyment
Students do not have to read challenging novels all the time. Reading for enjoyment can include:
The most important thing is that students read regularly and enjoy what they are reading.
Supporting Writing at Home
Good writing allows students to communicate their understanding clearly and effectively.
Encourage your child to plan before writing.
Ask them to read their work aloud.
Encourage proofreading for spelling and punctuation.
Discuss homework tasks before they start writing.
Encourage the use of subject-specific vocabulary.
Have you answered the question fully?
Can you explain your ideas in more detail?
Have you used key vocabulary?
Have you checked your spelling and punctuation?
Supporting Oracy at Home
Communication is a key life skill.
Students who are confident speakers often find it easier to explain ideas, participate in lessons and develop positive relationships.
Having regular conversations at home.
Asking your child to explain what they have learnt.
Discussing current events and topics of interest.
Encouraging them to justify their opinions.
Listening actively and asking follow-up questions.
Supporting Numeracy at Home
Numeracy is about much more than maths lessons. Students regularly use mathematical thinking in everyday life.
Everyday numeracy opportunities
Calculating discounts while shopping.
Measuring ingredients when cooking.
Estimating distances and travel times.
Managing pocket money or budgeting.
Supporting Sparx Maths
Please encourage your child to:
Complete their homework weekly.
Seek help when they are stuck.
Show resilience when solving problems.
Explain their mathematical thinking aloud.

Curriculum
Together, we transform lives through education.
Our mission is Together, we transform lives through education. We empower every student to achieve, belong, and participate, with an unwavering commitment to creating equitable opportunities and prioritising under-resourced students. We deliver this by having high expectations and standards, giving exceptional pastoral care and support and with an ambitious academic curriculum, which is rich and has breadth. This gives our students powerful knowledge enabling them to think for themselves and show strength of character, shaped by what they need to know, understand and fulfil, to have happy, successful and prosperous lives.
Purpose of the Curriculum
Our knowledge-rich curriculum is designed to be well-balanced and giving varied opportunities. It promotes the spiritual, moral, cultural, mental and physical development of our students and prepares them for the opportunities, responsibilities and experiences of adult life. Our aim is to provide a curriculum that is highly effective in delivering outcomes but also ensures our students will be widely educated, with experiences that include consideration of the best that humanity has produced; words, art, ideas, science. We aim to ensure that students leave The Castle School very well equipped for the next stage of their education, training or employment, and educated so that they enjoy life and live well.
The Curriculum Will:
We help ensure knowledge ‘sticks’. With careful design, sequencing, delivery and assessment students learn the curriculum not just encounter it.
Encourage independent learning and positive thinking amongst all students. Prepare them for life-long learning.
Where appropriate be personalised to meet the needs of individual students.
Build on the primary phase.
Ensure students are literate and numerate.
Ensure equity of access for all.
Reinforce kindness, empathy and celebrate equality and diversity.
We recognise that “the curriculum” is not just the timetabled lessons and that engagement in universal and choice enrichment opportunities is integral to our Personal Development Programme and school ethos. You can view all of the Personal Development documents below.
The school leadership constantly review and refine the curricular choices by engaging in regular discussion on ‘what’ to teach before considering ‘how’ to teach it. Leaders set an ambitious intent for their curriculum as we know that powerful knowledge is essential in realising the school’s ethos and vision. We acknowledge that the curriculum needs constant attention and refinement (ensuring it does not become a list of content). As a result it is always at the forefront of our thinking and must be considered and amended constantly, to ensure we teach the best that has been thought, said or written.
Examples Include:
In English, we want students to experience the wonder of Shakespeare, and to create deep, cognitive connections in their knowledge by exploring his stories, and the characters in those stories.
In Geography, students understand why the world is the way it is, so they can interpret earth’s human and physical landscapes. Students will develop an appreciation of the need to be empathetic global citizens who understand their responsibility toward the rest of humanity and the planet.
In Music, students experiment, rehearse and develop performance skills across a wide range of instruments including piano, keyboard, guitar and vocals, alongside a broad repertoire of music from Western Classical Tradition and the best popular music and music from around the world, developing an understanding of musical traditions in a variety of cultures, genres and historical periods. This musical journey allows students to understand and explore how music is created and communicated, including through the musical elements/inter-related dimensions: pitch, duration, dynamics, tempo, timbre, texture and musical notations.
Reading
“Books give a soul to the universe, wings to the mind, flight to the imagination, and life to everything.” Plato
At The Castle School reading is integral to our students’ education. We ensure students have opportunities to read regularly in all lessons and also during tutor time. Strategies for reading are used across the taught curriculum as well as the personal development programme, in tutor time and Personal, Social, Health and Economic (PSHE) education.
The Curriculum – Organisation
We do not believe in the pre-determined pathways that can limit students’ choice based on their ability, characteristics, or background. The universal curriculum gives students knowledge and information to make informed decisions about their curriculum, supported through thorough careers guidance at key times in a student’s five years at The Castle School.
High quality teaching is how knowledge can be assimilated through our well-sequenced curriculum model. Faculties work together to ensure that curriculum subject knowledge and the subject-specific pedagogy is central to the personalised and continued professional development that all our staff receive to ensure it has impact in the classroom, for every child, every day.
Throughout the five years, all students are taught core subjects: English, Mathematics, Science, Religious Education, PSHE, Careers and PE.
Key Stage 3 Offer
In Year 7, we build on the primary curriculum so that students acquire greater knowledge and language, developing skills and applying these to different situations. The breadth of subjects, 20 overall, with specialist teachers and facilities, so that children can explore practical subjects such as Art, Science, Dance, Drama, Music, Food, Design and Computing as well as access to a wide range of sports, will ignite a thirst to learn.
In Years 7 and 8, the students are divided into two equal ability populations for timetabling. These populations are mixed as students progress through the years so they can get to know a wider range of their peers. Setting is only in Maths in Year 7. In Year 8 English is also set. Setting in each subject is independent of that in other subjects. These sets are constantly reviewed and changes made whenever necessary. All other subjects are taught in mixed ability groups.
The opportunity to learn four languages, Mandarin, German, French and Spanish is part of the wider education beyond qualifications, as well as the full range of Arts subjects; Dance, Drama, Music, Art and Photography, which allows every child to develop his or her creativity. This richness and breadth is a key feature of our curriculum through the five years.
Subjects Years 7, 8 and 9
In addition to the core subjects, all students will also be taught all of the following to the end of year 9:
Humanities subjects: History and Geography.
Modern Foreign Languages: After a period of learning all four languages, students will choose one language from French, German, Mandarin and Spanish. Students in Year 9 have the opportunity of picking up a second language.
Arts: Art, Textiles, Dance, Drama and Music.
Design and Technology, Computing and Food.
PSHE education, which is taught via timetable enrichment days, tutor time, and across a range of curriculum subjects at various times throughout the year.
Students will also start their short course GCSE RE qualification in Year 9. This gives them an invaluable experience of what GCSE subjects and exams are like. They sit this in the summer of Year 10.
In January of Year 9, students will start the options process.
Key Stage 4 Offer
Students go on to study a rich and varied Key Stage 4 curriculum. The curriculum is filled with ambitious qualifications that match the drive to ensure that all our students achieve outstanding results to enable them to access their chosen pathway at Post 16.
The option process involves an Options Evening, GCSE taster lessons, explanatory videos and careers programme which support students with their choices.
Within the options, students will all continue to study at least one of either: History, Geography, Computing or a Modern Foreign Language. The options will vary from year to year, linked to the requests made by the cohort. All students complete short course RE in years 9 and 10.
Child Development (Cambridge Nationals)
Design and Technology

Engineering (Cambridge Nationals)

As well as their GCSE and vocational qualifications all students will have lessons, extended tutor times, assemblies, Curriculum Enrichment Days and PSHE lessons, delivered by our specialist team, in the following areas to fulfil our curriculum vision to further enrich their education at The Castle School. Depending on the context of the cohort, we may put on an early entry English Language GCSE. This enables students to achieve a GCSE early, boosting confidence going into Year 11.
Relationships Sex Education
Socially and culturally significant events, (for example, Black History Months, LGBTQ+ months)
Choice and targeted Enrichment
The Castle Challenge (Year 9)
Students are set in English, Maths and Science. The two top sets in Science have the opportunity to study triple Science. Part of this course includes a commitment to attending a lesson after school once a week. All other subjects have mixed ability classes.
Design Principles of The Castle School Curriculum and Sequencing
To ensure that our curriculum empowers our students, giving them the knowledge to make sense of the world and grow into citizens who make a difference, our curriculum has been carefully thought through and designed.
Our Heads of Faculty have designed and planned their curriculum according to the following principles:
Our curriculum is ambitious for all students, offering an exposure to the most powerful knowledge in each subject.
Our curriculum is sequenced so that new knowledge builds upon prior learning and students become increasingly fluent over time.
Our curriculum is detailed so that teachers are clear on what needs to be taught and when.
Our curriculum is taught to be remembered, not for coverage.
Our curriculum is supported with a literacy strategy that reinforces increased vocabulary acquisition and reading fluency.
Would you like more information on the curriculum? If so, please contact the school.
Homework
We believe that homework makes an invaluable contribution to students' progress and so we support them to find good independent learning habits either at home or in the school library with its extensive IT facilities. All homework is set through Arbor. Students can also access lesson resources and tasks via Microsoft Teams.

Free School Meals
Eligibility
Children who attend a Somerset County Council school, whose parents or carers receive certain benefits, may be entitled to free school meals.
Only the benefits listed here – and no other benefits – qualify you for free school meals for your children.
These are the benefits.
Employment and Support Allowance (Income related) – not Contribution related
Income-based Job Seekers Allowance (IBJSA) – not Contribution based
Guaranteed Element of State Pension Credit
Support under Part 6 of the Immigration and Asylum Act 1999
Child Tax Credit with an annual taxable income (as assessed by HMRC) of less than £16,190, as long as the family is not also in receipt of Working Tax Credit
If you have recently become unemployed, but are still receiving Working Tax Credits, you may be entitled to free school meals. Please contact Somerset Council on 0300 123 2244 for advice.
Apply Online
You can apply online for free school meals by following this link to the Somerset County Council website and submitting an application form. You can print a copy of the application form for free school meals and send it to the following address: Entitlements Team, County Hall, Taunton, TA1 4DY.
You do not need to send evidence with this application. If we need evidence later, we will ask you for it.
Apply in Person at our School Reception
You will need to supply the following details so that the school can assess your application:
• Your National Insurance Number / NASS number (can be found on your benefit letters)
• Your date of birth
• Your child(ren)'s details
If you have any questions about applying for free school meals, please contact us.
Changes to Your Benefit Entitlement
Please contact the school immediately if your benefit changes or ends, as it may mean that you no longer qualify to claim free school meals. If it is found that you did not notify us that you were no longer entitled to claim free school meals, you will be invoiced for the cost of all school meals taken free to which your child(ren) were not entitled.
